description: Known-Answer Test vectors for the trust snapshot: BOTH the content digest (the value digest_hex carries, which consumers pin) and the signing input (the bytes the detached signature covers). A conforming implementation in ANY language MUST reproduce every expected_* value byte-for-byte.

provenance.generator: an independent Python implementation sharing no code with either the signer or this verifier. Written 2026-08-12 in a fresh context from canonicalization_rules and the vector inputs alone; the reference implementation, every expected_* value, and every canonical byte fragment were withheld from its author.
provenance.independent_at: the ENCODER **and** the SCHEMA layer, for POSITIVE vectors. On 2026-08-12 an implementation written with no sight of any existing implementation, no expected_* values and no canonical byte fragments reproduced all 30 positive-vector outputs across both artifacts — body digest, signing input and signature — byte-for-byte. The field sets were therefore DERIVED from these rules, not transcribed. This supersedes the earlier caveat that the schema layer was untested.
provenance.NOT_independent_at: the NEGATIVE vectors. Traps are specified in prose rather than in bytes: no trap names its base vector, cascade behaviour (a body-only mistake changing digest, signing input and signature) is unstated, and trapA_declaration_order cannot be reproduced from this document at all — no struct declaration order appears in it, and rule 1 explicitly disclaims the field lists as orderings. NONE of the wrong_* values was reproduced or checked by the 2026-08-12 run.
provenance.evidence: 2026-08-06: a third implementation (Node/Go) written blind from canonicalization_rules alone diverged on the body field set — it included id and prev_bundle_id. See trapD_body_superset; rule 3 now enumerates the body field set. 2026-08-12: a second blind run (Python, fresh context) reproduced every positive vector in BOTH artifacts byte-for-byte on the first attempt, with 20 further values confirmed transitively. It raised 14 graded specification ambiguities — see the generator's accompanying notes — of which the negative vectors and the unstated signature encoding are the material ones. Building the blind package took four attempts: the first three leaked answers through digest_hex, wrong_signing_input_utf8 and wrong_body_utf8.
provenance.what_would_be_stronger: a third party, in a third language, working from canonicalization_rules with no sight of the expected_* values. The 2026-08-12 run met the second and third conditions but not the first.

canonicalization_rules: Object keys are emitted in SORTED (lexicographic by UTF-8 byte) order, NOT struct/field declaration order. Every field list stated in these rules is in declaration order for readability; NONE is an emission order.
The domain tag is emitted as a member whose KEY IS THE LITERAL STRING "domain", in both canonical forms.
BODY DIGEST field set, exactly: domain (= body_domain), id, issued_ms, issuer_ids, prev_snapshot_id. digest_hex is excluded because including it would be circular.
SIGNING INPUT field set, exactly: domain (= sig_domain), id, issued_ms, issuer_ids, digest_hex, prev_snapshot_id.
prev_snapshot_id is ALWAYS PRESENT with JSON null when there is no predecessor, in BOTH forms. The struct's own Serialize omits it (skip_serializing_if); the canonical forms do NOT.
Compact separators: no whitespace between tokens. NO trailing newline (Go's json.Encoder.Encode appends one; strip it).
No HTML escaping: '<', '>', '&' are emitted literally (Go must call Encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)).
'/' is NOT escaped (both domain tags contain one).
All hex is LOWERCASE. digest_hex is embedded in the signing input as a string, so its case is load-bearing.
issued_ms is a JSON integer (unsigned 64-bit), never a float or string. Values above 2^53 are exercised by a vector.
issuer_ids is a JSON array in the given order (arrays are NOT sorted). An empty set is [] -- never null, never omitted.
issuer ids are restricted at registration to [A-Za-z0-9._-] or are DIDs, so no canonical field here can carry U+2028/U+2029 -- the characters Go escapes even with SetEscapeHTML(false).

signing_key.note: 32-byte seed, every byte = 0x03. Public conformance material.

vectors.name: v1_first_snapshot_prev_none
vectors.note: First-ever snapshot: prev_snapshot_id is null in BOTH the body digest and the signing input.

vectors.name: v2_chained_snapshot_prev_some
vectors.note: Chained snapshot: prev_snapshot_id is a string.

vectors.name: v3_empty_issuer_set
vectors.note: Every issuer revoked: issuer_ids is []. Reachable, and a Go nil slice encodes as null rather than [].

vectors.name: v4_integers_above_2_53
vectors.note: issued_ms exceeds 2^53. A JavaScript verifier using JSON.parse rounds this silently.

negative_vectors.name: trapA_declaration_order
negative_vectors.why: Keys in struct/macro order instead of sorted. A naive Go struct produces this.

negative_vectors.name: trapB_omitempty_prev
negative_vectors.why: prev_snapshot_id dropped because the impl mirrored the struct's on-disk Serialize (skip_serializing_if / omitempty) instead of signing_input's always-present null. Only differs at the FIRST snapshot.

negative_vectors.name: trapC_body_digest_without_domain
negative_vectors.why: Body digest computed without the domain tag — the pre-2026-08-08 shape, which also used key 'prev' and omitted id.
